originalTitle: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations

content: “We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company’s third quarter earnings call. By Thursday, the company’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected. Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in company history,” Kress told investors. “Our momentum is real,” Kress said. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.” But investors are still trying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future. The company’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The New York Times. Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession plan — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on. It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia. On October 29th, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.” Nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June. The stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the new class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64. Then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a company-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang said he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025. The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee. Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the company’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year. On December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd. Retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research. chineseSummary: 英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二晚在结束这家陷入困境的芯片公司第三季度财报电话会议时表示：“我们已经做到了。”到周四，该公司的股价徘徊在每股 150 美元左右，较 10 月 6 日的历史高点下跌近 40%，并抹去了短暂的财报后 […]
chineseContent: 英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二晚在结束这家陷入困境的芯片公司第三季度财报电话会议时表示：“我们已经做到了。”到周四，该公司的股价徘徊在每股 150 美元左右，较 10 月 6 日的历史高点下跌近 40%，并消除了周二晚间财报发布后短暂的上涨。与此同时，随着 Anthropic 以每股 111.50 美元的价格在纳斯达克上市，华尔街正在为 Nvidia 最大的客户之一付出代价——比预期高出 34%。仅从收益报告数据来看，英伟达的季度业绩表现出色。在数据中心收入增长 110% 并超出华尔街预期的推动下，第三季度收入较去年同期增长一倍多，达到 1,158 亿美元。克雷斯告诉投资者，近 200 亿美元的收入来自备受期待的 Vera Rubin 平台，该平台在本季度发货，成为“公司历史上最快的产品增长”。 “我们的势头是真实的，”克雷斯说。 “凭借市场领先的多年路线图、延续到本世纪末的供应协议以及可持续的需求，我们完全有能力加速 Nvidia 的领导地位。”但投资者仍在试图调和英伟达近期出色的财务业绩和作为人工智能经济核心支柱的地位，同时对其未来表示严重担忧。最近几周，该公司的股价大幅下跌。据《纽约时报》援引美国情报消息人士称，由于对人工智能泡沫的担忧，芯片股在整个市场遭到抛售，该股首先受到市场抛售的推动，而在前首席执行官黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职后，该股再次受到打击，其中包括与一名涉嫌中国间谍的婚外情。哈维·琼斯 (Harvey Jones)，Nvidia 的新成员
